newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish official predicts 200mln punt EBR undershoot.
newsitem.headline: Irish official predicts 200mln punt EBR undershoot.

text.p: The Irish Exchequer may be at least 200 million punts better off at the end of the year than was forecast in the budget, Paddy Mullarkey, secretary of the Department of Finance, said on Thursday.

"It may be 200 million punts better off at least -- but there is a long way to go to the end of the year," he told a parliamentary committee. The government's full-year Exchequer Borrowing Requirement (EBR) target is 729 million punts.
Mullarkey and his officials were briefing the Finance and General Affairs committee about the economy and the preparations for the 1997 Budget.
Mullarkey also said the Ireland's debt/GDP ratio, on a Maastricht basis, was expected to fall to around 76 percent from 81.6 percent at the end of 1995.
He said the Irish economy had been growing three times faster than the EU average for the past five years and strong growth has continued this year.
Employment had risen by 90,000 in the past two years and this year another 40,000 jobs would be created, Mullarkey said.
He said he confidently expected the 1996 budget targets to be met by a safe margin, thanks to the higher than expected growth in tax revenues.
That tax growth is expected to continue in 1997.
Tax cuts in the last three budgets had been essential in getting national pay agreements and would be crucial if that progress was to be built on in 1997.
